title: NSPM-11: Artificial Intelligence in the National Security Enterprise
summary: NSPM-11 establishes a framework for adopting advanced AI across defense and intelligence while emphasizing secure systems, assurance, acquisition, talent, high-security compute, and resilient supply chains. It moves the discussion from general AI leadership toward controlled operational adoption.
key_findings: National-security AI adoption is tied to security, reliability, testing, assurance, and accountable governance.
High-security compute environments and sensitive-data handling are foundational infrastructure requirements.
Acquisition, workforce, and supply-chain resilience are treated as adoption constraints.
why_it_matters: It provides a policy bridge between frontier AI capability and the institutional systems needed to use it in high-consequence settings.
ftfn_relevance: Supports tracking secure compute, assurance, procurement, talent, and supply chains as AI dependencies.
Creates an implementation watch lane for standards, acquisition actions, and agency adoption evidence.
evidence_limits: The memorandum directs future implementation and does not prove agency deployment or system performance.
National-security details may be classified and therefore absent from public evidence.
